summary: A fixed three-bank determinant ratio and uniformly nondegenerate Schur-translated pure-triangle curvature do not alone imply a universal density bound. For three independent 2D unit-uniform banks, B=epsilon I2 and C=E=sqrt(epsilon) I2 give determinant ratio 1 and E B^{-1} C=I2, while the quadratic output is supported in an interval of length at most 6 sqrt(epsilon), hence its density norm is at least 1/(6 sqrt(epsilon)). This is not an s8 or QFORM counterexample because the full terminal spectral-saturation hypotheses are absent.
